question_text: Why are spokes provided in a bicycle wheel?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 7 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What spokes do
lines: Spokes connect the rim to the axle, so
most of the wheel’s mass sits at the
rim. This increases the moment of
steps.margin_note: The phrase that earns the mark is "increases the moment of inertia".
steps.why: Moment of inertia grows as mr² — the same mass placed farther from the axis resists changes of rotation more. Spokes let the wheel be light AND have its mass at the rim.
common_mistakes: Saying spokes are only for strength. The examiner wants the moment-of-inertia reason.

recall.must_convey: That spokes concentrate the mass at the rim, increasing the moment of inertia.

steps.memory_tip: Spokes let the mass sit at the rim — in mr², a larger r means a larger moment of inertia.

steps.label: The result
lines: A large moment of inertia resists
sudden changes in rotation, so the
steps.margin_note: Close on the smooth, steady motion — that is what the question is really asking about.
steps.why: The board words this as "ensures uniform speed". The honest mechanism is rotational inertia smoothing out small jerks from the road and the pedalling — the wheel resists CHANGES, it does not create uniformity by itself.
common_mistakes: Stopping at "moment of inertia increases" without saying what that does for the ride.

recall.must_convey: That the large moment of inertia makes the rotation smooth and steady.

steps.memory_tip: A large I resists changes in rotation, so the wheel turns steadily between pedal strokes.
